new_public_evidence.source: Finke, Johansen, Lee, Murray, Resampling in conditional SMC algorithms
new_public_evidence.result: Their rho/lambda/phi framework gives explicit post-resampling proper weights for dependent resampling and proves valid SMC normalizing-constant estimation under proper weighting plus persistence.

derived_results.claim: With expected offspring count r_n=sum_m P(A^m=n) and balanced index distribution, Finke's post-resampling weight simplifies to W_n/r_n. If r_n=Mq_n for a defensive priority proposal q, every selected child gets exactly W_n/(Mq_n), even when sibling ancestor indices are dependent.

The r120 one-step stratified priority mechanism extends recursively: defensive q, stratified expected counts Mq, balanced W/(Mq) postweights, base transition/potential, normalize, repeat. Proper weighting handles sibling dependence; the support floor provides the required positive selection support.

Priority scores and q may depend on the current weighted particle system before current resampling randomness, so semantic/proxy prefix features can steer the next descendants while preserving the proper-weighting formula.

Ancestor correction W/(Mq) does not correct environment/tool responses sampled from a proposal Q. Any departure from base transition P still needs P/Q likelihood ratios or a narrower identifiable target.

engineering_update.scope: Recursive correctness follows the cited proper-weighting framework when the actual resampling law/index distribution matches the balanced Mq construction. Efficiency remains empirical.

negative_or_scope_evidence: Do not use W/(Mq) for an arbitrary resampler whose expected counts are not Mq or whose index distribution is not balanced.
Correct normalizing-constant expectation does not imply low variance.

Verify both estimators match the exact normalizing constant within Monte Carlo error, then quantify variance/ESS across 2-5 generations.
